name: Naharai
overview: Naharai was a male warrior known as the Beerothite and was counted as the thirty-fourth member of "the thirty," an elite group of King David's mighty men. Beyond this designation, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribal affiliation or personal background. His inclusion among David's renowned warriors highlights his role in the king's military exploits.
namesAndTitles: The name Naharai appears only once in Scripture without a provided meaning or title significance. It is simply recorded as a proper name in 2 Samuel 23:37.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Naharai beyond what is indicated by his designation as a Beerothite and his membership among David's mighty men.
scriptureSignificance: Naharai's significance lies in his membership among "the thirty," the elite warriors who supported King David during his reign. Being identified as a Beerothite connects him to the city of Beeroth, indicating his geographic origin. His mention in the biblical record underscores the diverse composition of David's loyal fighters and contributes to the historical understanding of David's military leadership.
